text:
### Observed differences

- The choice between two alternative activity blocks reversed. In the earlier window, A24, A25 and A26 each ran in about 82 in 100 traces and typically together (all three co-occurring in about 82 in 100 traces), while A21, A22 and A23 each ran in only about 19 in 100 traces. In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 each run in about 79 in 100 traces (all three together in about 79 in 100), while A24, A25 and A26 each run in only about 21 in 100. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL015, REL023, REL036, REL041]
- The two blocks remained mutually exclusive in both windows: cross-block pairs such as A21–A24, A22–A25 or A23–A26 occur in the same trace in at most about 1 in 100 cases before and after, so the exclusive structure itself is intact and only the preferred alternative changed. [REL017, REL019, REL024, REL026, REL030, REL032]
- A20 precedes whichever block runs: in the earlier window A20 was followed by A24–A26 in about 81 in 100 traces; in the later window A20 is followed by A21–A23 in about 78 in 100 traces. The order among A21, A22 and A23 stays mixed (both orders in similar shares) in both windows. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL023]
- Downstream activities switched which block they accompany. A30 occurs in essentially every trace in both windows; it co-occurred with A24–A26 in about 82 in 100 earlier traces but now co-occurs with A21–A23 in about 79 in 100. A32 and A33 shifted from co-occurring mainly with A24–A26 (about 52 in 100) to co-occurring mainly with A21–A23 (about 56 in 100). [REL020, REL027, REL033, REL038, REL021, REL028, REL039, REL046]
- A10 became rarer and its placement more variable: it appeared in about 17 in 100 traces before versus about 7 in 100 after, and its mean relative position dropped from about 0.86 to about 0.52 with a much wider spread (standard deviation about 0.28 versus 0.03). [POS001, REL001, REL004]
- A02 rose from about 2 in 100 traces to about 9 in 100 (4 versus 18 traces). [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the exclusive choice between two existing alternative paths flipped: in the earlier window traces usually executed the A24–A25–A26 block after A20 (about 82 in 100 traces) and rarely the A21–A23 block (about 19 in 100), whereas in the later window A20 is usually followed by A21, A22 and A23 executed together (about 79 in 100 traces) while A24–A26 run in only about 21 in 100 traces. [OCC002, OCC005, REL009, REL012, REL015, REL017, REL024, REL030, REL036]

Supporting signs: 56 control-flow items qualified, roughly 80 times the about 0.7 expected for an unchanged process, so the pattern as a whole is not what random re-splits of these windows produce; each item also differs more than in about 99.5 in 100 reference comparisons. [screening] The change is shown directly by relational evidence, is consistent across every pair within and between the two blocks, and meets the conditions for a shift in how often existing paths are taken: both blocks are observed in substantial shares in both windows (about 19–82 in 100), only the selection shares move, and exclusivity, within-block togetherness and the precedence of A20 are preserved. [REL009, REL015, REL017, REL023, REL024, REL036, REL041] The downstream realignment of A30, A32 and A33 toward the now-dominant block fits the same flip. [REL020, REL021, REL027, REL028, REL038, REL039]

Limitation: the precedence of A20 is established only by co-occurrence and order shares, as the evidence contains no direct successor items, so an untested activity between A20 and the blocks could be the actual point where the branch is selected; the exact shares also carry the sampling uncertainty of two 200-trace windows. [REL009, REL012]

Other differences:
- A10 appears in fewer traces (about 17 in 100 down to about 7 in 100) and, when it occurs, at a lower and much more variable relative position; a lag item further suggests the distance from A32 to A10 spread from mostly one step to one-to-three steps, but it rests on only 4 after-window observations. [POS001, LAG001, REL001, REL004]
- A02 participation rose from about 2 in 100 to about 9 in 100 traces, a difference based on small counts (4 versus 18 traces). [OCC001]
